title: Beef Rendang
subtitle: Slow-cooked dry Malaysian beef curry
excerpt: Beef shin braised for three hours in coconut milk and a spice paste of lemongrass, chilli, galangal, and turmeric until the liquid is completely absorbed and the meat is coated in a dark, rich paste.

recipe.sourceNotes: Rendang is a dish of Minangkabau origin from West Sumatra in Indonesia, now central to Malaysian and Indonesian cuisines. It is one of the most complex curries in Southeast Asian cooking, requiring a long, patient reduction of spiced coconut milk until almost no liquid remains and the beef is coated in a concentrated, deeply flavoured paste. True rendang takes three to four hours to make and is intended to be a preserved food, which is why it is cooked until dry. Wet rendang, where the coconut milk is only partially reduced, is a shortcut version. The dish has been popular in Britain since the 1980s, introduced through Singaporean and Malaysian restaurants.

content.text: The cooking happens in three stages. In the first stage the beef braises in the coconut milk and spice paste until cooked through. In the second stage the liquid evaporates and the spices begin to fry. In the third stage the beef and the concentrated dry paste fry in the released coconut oil, building deep brown caramelised edges. Do not rush the final stage or the rendang will be pale.

bruised and tied in a knot

content.text: Blend the chilli, shallots, garlic, ginger, and dried spices with a splash of water to form a smooth paste.
Heat the oil in a large, wide pan. Fry the spice paste for 5 minutes, stirring constantly, until fragrant and darkening slightly.
Add the beef, coconut milk, lemongrass, toasted desiccated coconut, and salt. Bring to a simmer. Cook uncovered over medium-low heat for 1 hour 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.

Reduce to low heat. Cook for a further 1 to 1 hour 30 minutes, stirring more frequently as the liquid reduces, until the coconut milk has almost completely evaporated and the beef is coated in a dark, oily paste. The beef will begin to fry in the released coconut oil. Stir constantly at this stage to prevent burning. Remove the lemongrass. Serve with steamed rice.
